אפרת ואח - אלון. במכתב תנחומים למשפחה השכולה כתב מפקדו: "למרות התקופה הקצרה בה שהה עימנו למדנו להוקיר את תכונותיו היפות את מרצו הרב, נחישותו ודבקותו במטרה, מחד-גיסא ויחסו האנושי והדאגה שגילה כלפי פקודיו, מאידך-גיסא. ועוד הוסיף "דמותו של אמיר מהווה עבורנו סמל של לוחם אמיץ ונמרץ". מחנכו מבית-הספר ע"ש הימלפרב כתב על שאיפתו לשלמות, על רצונו העז להצליח ועל היותו אדם של אמת ואמונה, בעל תאוות ידע ואהבה לארץ. חברי קהילת בית-הכנסת 'מנחם ציון' שברובע היהודי בעיר העתיקה בירושלים, הנציחו את זכרו בבית-מדרש שנפתח על שמו. חבריו ליחידה בחיל הצנחנים הוציאו חוברת זיכרון לזכרו ובה דברי זיכרון פרי עטם ותצלומים רבים. מרכז זלמן שז"ר לתולדות עם ישראל, המנוהל על-ידי אביו, הקדיש את סידרת הרומנים ההיסטוריים לבני הנעורים לזכרו של סגן אמיר יקותיאל. כמו-כן הוציא המרכז לזכרו קובץ מאמרים בנושא "קדושת החיים וחירוף נפש בתולדות ישראל ובמחשבת ישראל", בעריכת פרופ' אבי רביצקי ופרופ' ישעיהו גפני. במקום נפילתו ליד הבור שאליו נפל באזור מערות בית גוברין הקימו חייליו אנדרטה לזכרו. את השיר "בן יקיר לי" שנכתב והולחן לזכרו של אמיר ז"ל, על ידי מלכי בן ימין טפרברג, גיסתה של אחותו של אמיר ז"ל, בהשראת דברים שנאמרו על קברו על ידי אביו באזכרה במלאת 25 שנים לנפילתו. השיר מבוצע על ידי ישי ריבו.

Amir (Kuti) Yekutiel, son of Haya and Tzvi, was born on 29 Tishrei 5728 (2 October 1967) in Jerusalem. He was the firstborn son of his parents. He studied at the state religious elementary school "Dugma LeBanim" named after Uziel, and continued at the Himmelfarb high school. He was a member of the Bnei Akiva youth movement, and at the same time was active in Gadna Air, due to his strong desire to become a pilot in the Air Force. Within this framework he took part in circles and camps held at Air Force bases, and developed meaningful friendships with many secular friends.

At the end of his high school studies, in the summer of 1985, the family left for a sabbatical year in the United States, where his father did research at Harvard University in Boston. Because Amir's enlistment was deferred due to his young age, he was able to use this time for external studies at the university. In January 1986, in the middle of the sabbatical year, he returned to Israel, enlisted in the IDF, and was posted to serve in the Air Force. He volunteered for a pilot course and studied in it for about five months. He then volunteered to serve in the Paratroopers Brigade. Within this framework he went through a training track for squad commanders and was sent to an officers' course, after which he returned to command at the squad commanders' school.

Amir fell on 4 Tishrei 5749 (15 September 1988) while carrying out his duties, in an accident on a training range in the Me'arot Beit Guvrin area, and was laid to rest in the military cemetery on Mount Herzl in Jerusalem. He was posthumously promoted to the rank of Lieutenant. He is survived by his parents, his sister Efrat and his brother Alon.

In a letter of condolence to the bereaved family, his commander wrote: "Despite the short period in which he was with us, we learned to appreciate his fine qualities, his great zeal, his determination and devotion to his goal, on the one hand, and his human attitude and the care he showed toward his subordinates, on the other." He added: "Amir's image is for us a symbol of a brave and energetic fighter."

His teacher from the Himmelfarb school wrote of his aspiration for perfection, his strong desire to succeed, and his being a person of truth and faith, with a thirst for knowledge and a love for the land. Members of the "Menachem Tzion" synagogue community in the Jewish Quarter of the Old City of Jerusalem commemorated his memory with a study hall named after him. His comrades in the Paratroopers Brigade published a memorial booklet in his memory, containing remembrances written by them and many photographs. The Zalman Shazar Center for Jewish History, directed by his father, dedicated its series of historical novels for young readers to the memory of Lieutenant Amir Yekutiel. The Center also published, in his memory, a collection of essays on "The Sanctity of Life and Self-Sacrifice in Jewish History and Jewish Thought," edited by Prof. Avi Ravitzky and Prof. Yeshayahu Gafni.

At the site where he fell, next to the pit into which he fell in the Me'arot Beit Guvrin area, his soldiers erected a monument in his memory. The song "Ben Yakir Li" ("My Dear Son"), written and composed in his memory by Malki Ben Yamin Tepperberg, sister-in-law of Amir's sister, was inspired by words spoken at his grave by his father at a memorial service marking 25 years since his fall. The song is performed by Yishai Ribo.
